judged_text: The webhook picks the credential to overwrite with findFirst on (userId, appId) with no orderBy and no uniqueness guarantee, even though re-installing an app creates multiple credential rows for the same user and app. When a user has more than one credential for the app, the sync updates an arbitrary row — the credential actually used by bookings keeps its expired keys, so the sync silently no-ops for that user while the handler reports success.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler (`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`), the credential row to update is selected via `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId: reqBody.userId, appId: appMetadata.slug } })` with no `orderBy` and no evidence in this diff of a uniqueness constraint on `(userId, appId)`. If multiple credential rows can exist for the same user/app, the code would update an arbitrary row and report success. However, the diff does not show the Prisma schema or any behavior proving duplicates are possible, so the "re-installing creates multiple rows" claim cannot be verified from the diff alone; the review point is still valid as a determinism/data-integrity concern for this new logic.
